I reviewed the retrieved telemetry (HTTP 200, 28 figures, generated 2026-10-20). No instruction-like content was found embedded in the figure text itself — all entries are standard data/source descriptions, so there is no prompt-injection finding to report here. Below is the public brief drawing only on the figures provided, avoiding causal claims between price and attention series, and flagging that encyclopedia-attention comparisons share a broad decline confound.

**Brief:** Consumer prices moved higher across most tracked categories over the past year: apparel CPI rose 3.4% (index 135.4 → 140.0), shelter CPI rose 3.2% (index 418.6 → 432.1), energy CPI rose 20.4%, and food CPI rose 2.5%, while egg prices fell from $3.49 to $2.27/doz and electricity rose from $0.19 to $0.20/kWh. Encyclopedia attention moved differently across topics — "Renting" pageviews fell 10.7% and "Electric vehicle" fell 21.8%, while "Athleisure" rose 18.6% — but these are separate measurements from the price indexes, not explanations for them, and since pageviews have broadly declined across many topics, a falling number does not necessarily mean reduced public interest. The most-viewed topic in each category was Haute couture (24,424 views) for clothing, Solar panel (16,270) for energy, Fast food (14,998) for food, and Apartment (9,200) for shelter. Separately, a local OpenStreetMap scan found 166 gathering places in the sampled area, the most common kind being Places of worship (102).
